## Automated Tests Required

### Action UI — Logic (secondary, extractable pure functions)
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/action_ui/action_ui_formatting_test.gd`

**What to test** (from the GDD's Acceptance Criteria — Number Formatting + Progress Bar sections):

*Number formatting boundaries:*
- 847 → `"847"`
- 999 → `"999"`
- 1,000 → `"1.0K"` (inclusive lower bound — the critical boundary test)
- 28,412 → `"28.4K"`
- 999,999 → `"999.9K"`
- 1,000,000 → `"1.0M"` (hard boundary)
- 1,250,000 → `"1.3M"`

*Progress bar fill_ratio:*
- elapsed_time=0, duration=D>0 → fill_ratio=0
- 0<elapsed_time<duration → fill_ratio=clamp(E/D, 0, 1)
- elapsed_time≥duration → fill_ratio=1 (clamped, never exceeds)

**Edge cases to cover** (from the GDD's Defined Edge Cases section):
- Negative Zasięgi/Sponsorzy value → displayed as-is, no UI-layer clamping (do NOT add a defensive clamp that isn't in the spec)
- A locked slot with `unlock_threshold=null` → generic 🔒, no number rendered (logic-testable: does the formatter get called at all for null thresholds?)

**Estimated test count**: ~10 unit tests (7 formatting boundary cases + 3 fill_ratio cases)

**Important implementation note for `/dev-story`**: extract number-formatting and fill_ratio calculation into pure static functions (e.g. a new `ActionUIFormatting` utility class, following the `ResourceFormulas` precedent from the Resource System epic) BEFORE wiring them into any Control node. This is what makes them testable without a scene tree — write and test the pure functions first, then call them from the actual UI scene's script.

**Out of scope for automated tests** (per the GDD's own "Not testable against this GDD alone" section): actual `unlock_threshold` values (no source of truth yet), Main Navigation/Screen Flow transitions (undesigned), exact truncation length (implementation-defined, no concrete value yet), Juice/Feedback System effects (undesigned), `duration=0` (violates Action System's own invariant — not this GDD's behavior to test).

## Manual QA Checklist

### Action UI — UI (primary: layout, slot state, button enable/disable)
**Verification method**: Manual step-through in the Godot editor (run the scene directly), screenshot evidence
**Who must sign off**: solo dev
**Evidence to capture**: screenshots of each state (idle/running, locked/unlocked slots, overlay visible/hidden)

Checklist (every UI acceptance criterion translated into a manual check item):
- [ ] Screen renders exactly 3 zones: Resource HUD, Action Grid, Running Action Overlay (conditional)
- [ ] Resource HUD shows all 5 resources simultaneously; Morale shows a band label (High/Normal/Low/Critical), not a raw percentage
- [ ] Action Grid renders exactly 6 slots: 3 unlocked + 3 locked
- [ ] A slot unlocking does NOT add/remove/reposition any slot — the same slot switches 🔒→active in place (test by simulating a milestone-unlock state change)
- [ ] `idle` state: all 3 unlocked buttons enabled; tapping one sends the choice to Action System; tapping a locked slot is a no-op with no visible change
- [ ] `running` state: all 6 buttons disabled; tapping any button is a no-op
- [ ] `running→resolved→idle` transition: overlay hides, unlocked buttons re-enable
- [ ] Overlay shows action name and remaining time alongside the progress bar
- [ ] An action name exceeding button width truncates with an ellipsis; button dimensions stay unchanged
- [ ] Touch target sizing matches `technical-preferences.md`'s requirement (large, touch-friendly, no hover-only interaction) — verify on an actual touch-sized hit area, not just visually

*No subjective ("feels"/"looks") criteria in this GDD's Acceptance Criteria section — all UI criteria above are concrete and falsifiable as written.*

---

## Smoke Test Scope

1. Game launches to main menu without crash — **this sprint is the first time this becomes testable** (Boot/Main scene scaffolding is part of 6-1's prerequisite scope)
2. New game / new session can be started — first time testable this sprint
3. Action UI — primary mechanic this sprint: tap an unlocked action, confirm it starts, confirm the overlay/progress bar updates, confirm it resolves back to idle
4. Regression check: confirm `ActionSystem`'s existing signal contract (`action_completed`) still drives the UI correctly — this is the first real consumer of that signal outside of tests
5. Save / load cycle — N/A, no new SaveSystem changes this sprint (though Boot scene scaffolding will exercise `SaveSystem.load_save()` for the first time in a real scene, not just a test)
6. Performance — first real frame-budget check this project: confirm the progress bar's per-frame update (GDD requires it "every frame, not throttled") stays within the 16.6ms budget on whatever hardware is available

---

## Playtest Requirements

No formal multi-session playtest required for this sprint — Action UI's acceptance criteria are concrete and falsifiable (see Manual QA Checklist above), not subjective "does it feel good" questions. A single manual walkthrough by the developer is sufficient evidence.

If, after implementation, the screen's overall feel raises new questions not covered by the GDD's criteria (e.g., "is the touch target big enough to feel good, not just meet the spec"), flag that as a candidate for a future Vertical Slice playtest — not blocking for this sprint.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified — automated test result (formatting/fill_ratio) OR documented manual evidence (layout/state/button behavior)
- [ ] Test file exists at `tests/unit/action_ui/action_ui_formatting_test.gd`
- [ ] Manual evidence document exists at `production/qa/evidence/action-ui-evidence.md`
- [ ] Smoke check passes (run `/smoke-check sprint` before QA hand-off) — first sprint where this actually exercises a real launchable scene
- [ ] No regressions introduced — particularly, confirm `ActionSystem`'s test suite (152+ tests) still passes unchanged after this sprint's UI work
- [ ] Code reviewed (via `/code-review`)
- [ ] Story file(s) updated to `Status: Complete` (via `/story-done`) — story files must be created first via `/create-epics action-ui` then `/create-stories action-ui`
